note: Recast from the soldier measurements and key of Bose 1999; the original is a faunistic work giving only measurements and distribution, without a morphological description, and the original description of this species (Roonwal & Sen-Sarma 1956) was not obtained in full for this batch, so this entry contains only measurements and the key's diagnostic points, with no morphological account. Measurements in millimetres.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Only 2 species of the genus occur in northeastern India, and the alates of both are unknown; the key separates them on soldier body size: in this species head length (to the mandibular base) 1.26 mm, maximum head width 1.08 mm, pronotum width 0.72 mm, whereas in P. shamimi these are 0.95—0.98, 0.85 and 0.50—0.53 mm respectively. The Arunachal Pradesh specimens examined by Bose have mandibles 0.65—0.75 mm long and pronotum 0.34—0.47 mm long, both larger than in P. shamimi (mandibles 0.63 mm, pronotum length 0.28 mm).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements by Bose 1999 for 5 soldiers from Arunachal Pradesh (mm): total body length about 3.5—3.75; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.60—1.70; head length (to the mandibular base) 1.18—1.30; maximum head width 1.00—1.12; mandible length 0.65—0.75; pronotum length 0.34—0.47, maximum width 0.65—0.70. The original gives no description of body colour, head shape, mandibular dentition or pilosity. Distribution: Nong Priang stream bank, Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, India (type locality), and Kameng and Upper Subansiri, Arunachal Pradesh.
